item.title: More than 1,000 arrested in France as protesters and police clash
item.description:
Nearly 1,000 people were arrested in nationwide protests in France, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said Saturday, after demonstrations over the high cost of living and the country's education system earlier in the day remained largely peaceful.
Nuñez said the number of arrests is expected to rise significantly. He said marches "passed off well" in cities, but police officers found themselves confronted with "an extremely elevated level of violence" from "ultra-left" groups later in the day. Nuñez said some shops and businesses had been looted, but "the scale was far smaller" than a week earlier, when some 3,000 businesses were damaged or looted.
He said police acted more rapidly and conducted more pre-demonstration checks. Businesses and shopping centers had also been better protected. Earlier Saturday, the interior minister said police had confiscated weapons including metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said.
The French Interior Ministry said about 410,000 people participated in about 298 protests around the country. Union organizers from the General Confederation of Labor put the number at around 800,000. An explanation for the discrepancy was not immediately available.
A protester waves the French flag near Porte de Vincennes during a demonstration in Paris on October 24, 2026.
Aris MESSINIS /AFP via Getty Images
Some confrontations were reported between authorities and demonstrators in several cities, but as of Saturday evening there had been no repeat of the major street violence and rioting that erupted amid similar protests last week.

item.title: 1 arrested after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest mountain retreat
item.description:
A suspect has been arrested in Germany following a fire at Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat, known as Eagle's Nest, German police said.
Authorities were alerted to a fire at the Nazi leader's mountain residence on the peak of Obersalzberg at approximately 9:15 p.m. local time on Friday, Upper Bavaria South police said in a statement.
The building, also known as Kehlsteinhaus, was "completely engulfed in flames" when firefighters arrived, police said, but no one was found inside and no injuries were reported.
Fire trucks had some difficulty accessing the site "due to the local conditions," authorities added.
Still from a webcam of the Kehlsteinhaus early on Oct. 24, 2026, after a large fire broke out in the southern German state of Bavaria.
Berchtesgaden /AFP via Getty Images
"Shortly after the fire broke out, a suspect came into the focus of investigators," the statement said, adding that the cause of the fire is now under criminal investigation and one person was taken into custody.
The 33-year-old suspect, a German citizen who has ties to the Berchtesgaden area but doesn't currently live there, prosecutors said, has been questioned, The Associated Press reported. They said he showed signs of mental illness and he was being sent to a psychiatric facility, but they also would look into the possibility of a political motive in view of the building's history.
There were no current indications that anyone else was involved, police said.
At an elevation of 6,017 feet, Hitler's Eagle's Nest was completed in 1938 and occasionally used by the Nazi leader as a temporary seat of government. The site was spared from Allied bombing during World War II, largely preserving its original state.

item.title: Iran says U.S. military not allowed in Gulf "under any circumstance"
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran warned on Saturday that U.S. ships would never be allowed in the Persian Gulf "under any circumstances," as tensions between Tehran and Washington continue mounting. Both sides have signalled a possible return to strikes, with the U.S. ambassador to Turkey warning Iran could be struck as soon as this weekend.Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Friday that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad, with plots to kill Americans reaching "advanced stages" in the Middle East and other countries. U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz has told the Financial Times the war with Iran could last another year, but Waltz said he hopes the Iranians "come to the table" before that.
New Updates
1:40 PM / October 24, 2026
Ayatollah meets with head of Iranian judiciary, focuses on compensation for war damage
Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who has still not been seen in public since the beginning of the war, met with Hujjat al-Islam Mohseni Ejei, the head of Iran's judiciary, to discuss a range of issues on Saturday.
Most interestingly, in connection to the war, a readout of the meeting on X said Iran was committed to "resolutely pursuing compensation for material and moral damages arising from the crimes committed by" the U.S. and Israel.
One of Iran's demands in the past as part of a peace agreement was the U.S. would have to pay to rebuild much of the damage in the country. The demand was dismissed by the U.S.
While not specific, the statement also said they discussed "making the fullest possible use of modern technologies."

item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX throttled Ukraine Starlink speeds over drone strikes
item.description:
Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.
Musk's admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week.
Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.
"The speeds are now where they need to be," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that restoration began overnight and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving front-line logistics and defense against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Oct. 22, 2026.
Ukrinform/NurPhoto via Getty Images
Musk admits he was behind Starlink's speed restriction
Before Musk's confirmation, questions persisted last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Ukraine has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.
President Trump had said he didn't make the call, while also saying Musk should not be blamed. On Tuesday, CBS News reported that Musk was behind the disruption.
In a post Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX throttled the Starlink satellite internet service.

item.title: Deadly shooting in Paris suburb investigated as terrorism, officials say
item.description:
A gunman shooting from his car killed one person and injured at least 5 others, including a 12-year-old girl, in the Paris suburb of Trappes on Friday, in what authorities described as a racially motivated act of terrorism.
President Emmanuel Macron called it "a racist terror attack" and said the suspect's statements suggested it was premeditated.
"These people were targeted because of their skin color or perceived religion, and for no other reason," Macron said following a meeting with officials and residents. "There is no place for this in France."
Prosecutors said they were investigating whether the acts targeted the "real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion" of the victims. They said they have opened an investigation for "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise."
The alleged shooter was "firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath" as he drove through Trappes and neighboring La Verriere, Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh told broadcaster BFMTV.
"This is probably one of the first attempted mass killings motivated by Islamophobia and racism," Rabeh told reporters, the Associated Press reported. "This was a terrorist attack with racist, likely Islamophobic, overtones."
Police officers at the scene of a shooting rampage that killed at least 1 in Trappes, a suburb of Paris, France, on Oct, 23, 2026.
Dimitar DILKOFF /AFP via Getty Images
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the suspect fired "what appears to have been a military-grade weapon, or at least an automatic weapon." Rabeh called it a "miracle" that there were not more casualties. Nuñez said the gunman "clearly" committed "a terrorist crime" that may have been racially motivated.

item.title: German man arrested for allegedly driving U.S. teen to die by suicide
item.description:
German police, acting on an FBI tip-off, arrested an alleged online sadist accused of driving a 14-year-old U.S. girl to hang herself, prosecutors said Friday.
The 18-year-old German was arrested in Hamburg on Thursday, accused of being the indirect perpetrator of murder and grievous bodily harm.
FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O'Malley said in a statement that their office worked with the Fort Wayne Police Department to provide information to the German police to help advance the arrest. The Fort Wayne Police Department said in a statement that its Homicide Unit identified a suspect who contributed to the juvenile's death.
"Anyone who targets or exploits a child should understand this: There is no safe haven from justice. It doesn't matter where you live or where you try to hide. The FBI will work with our partners around the world to find you and hold you accountable," O'Malley said.
The suspect was linked to an online group called "Nefarious Maniac Kult" or "NMK," part of a global network known by the labels "764" or "COM," the Hamburg public prosecutor's office said.
From September 2024 to September 2025, the FBI has seen a 300% increase in nihilistic violent extremism cases — many involving the 764 group, said FBI Director Kash Patel. The group 764 lacks a specific ideology, but members openly encourage self-harm and violence and encourage victims to produce videos documenting acts of self-harm or child sexual abuse material.
Between September and October, the suspect, then aged 17, allegedly "exerted influence" via the social network Discord over the girl from Indiana state whom prosecutors described as "psychologically fragile".
The suspect allegedly pressured the girl to cut herself and write the letters "NMK" on a wall in her own blood, and had her send him video recordings of these acts. A few days later, she hanged herself in her bedroom, prosecutors said.

item.title: U.K. police confirm it received letter with claims against Meghan's father
item.description:
A letter making a "number of claims" against the father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was received by the Metropolitan Police in 2019, a Scotland Yard spokesperson confirmed to CBS News on Saturday.
Police said they passed the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess "for their awareness," however, the details of the allegations made in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.
On Friday, it was reported that Meghan's estranged father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation by authorities in the Philippines for alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.
A spokesperson for the Philippine National Police told CBS News in a statement Saturday that they launched an investigation after Markle's personal items were turned over to law enforcement by his son, Thomas Markle Jr.
"At this point, investigators are looking into the nature and origin of the materials and whether these may be connected to any violation of law," Col. Allen Rae Co said in a statement. "U.S. authorities have also offered assistance should Philippine authorities determine that their support is needed as the investigation progresses."
The British tabloid The Sun was the first to report the allegations against Markle Sr. The report said the younger Markle allegedly discovered child abuse materials in storage boxes at his father's home in the Philippines.
